title: Understanding the Logistic Function
text: The logistic function, denoted as sigma, maps any real-valued number into the range $$(0,1)$$. This is crucial for logistic regression as it helps in predicting probabilities. Consider how the function behaves when the input value increases.

title: Comparing Exponents
text: When comparing $$\operatorname{\sigma}\left(X^T \beta\right)$$ and $$\operatorname{\sigma}\left(X^T 2\beta\right)$$, think about how doubling the coefficients in the exponent affects the value of the logistic function. Does it always increase, decrease, or vary?

title: Effect of Doubling Coefficients
text: What happens to the value of $$X^T \beta$$ when beta is doubled?

title: Behavior of the Logistic Function
text: The logistic function is non-linear and its rate of change depends on the input value. Consider how this non-linearity might affect the comparison between $$\operatorname{\sigma}\left(X^T \beta\right)$$ and $$\operatorname{\sigma}\left(X^T 2\beta\right)$$.
